 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SANDEEP N. BHATT  Date : 13/09/2024  ORAL JUDGMENT NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4759/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant - Insurance Company, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 26.07.2023 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Rajkot in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.470 of 2015, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.15,43,600/-
with 9% per annum interest from the date of filing claim petition till its realization, to the claimant/s, holding Opponents No1 and 2 i.e. owner and insurance company of the Jeep bearing registration No.GJ-10-W-1958 liable, jointly and several.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.470 of 2015
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case, as per claimant/s, are as under :
2.1

That on 22.11.2014 at about 6:30 p.m., near sign board of village Khaydi on Lalpur - Jamnagar Highway, accident occurred between the Jeep bearing registration No.GJ-10-W-1958 and Car bearing registration No.GJ-10-BG- 6370.
As a result, deceased - Jayeshbhai Karanbhai Nandaniya sustained serious injuries and ultimately, the deceased succumbed to the injuries.

Therefore, the legal heirs of the deceased - widow, mother and brother have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.50 lakhs with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the present NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4759/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponent No.1 - owner of the Jeep has appeared, but not filed any written statement contesting claim petition.
Opponent No.2 - Insurance Company has appeared and filed its written statement / objections, by disputing all the averments made by the claimants in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the appellant - insurance company of the Jeep (original opponent No.2).

sentences.text: 2 3. Learned advocate Mr. Rathin Raval for the appellant - insurance company - original opponent No.2 has fairly submitted that there is no dispute with regard to the quantum decided by the Tribunal.

He has also fairly NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4759/2023 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/09/2024 undefined submitted that there is no dispute with regard to the general and non-pecuniary damages awarded by the Tribunal to the claimants.
He has submitted that the only dispute is with regard to the negligence.

He has submitted that the learned advocate for the claimants has submitted a purshis at Exh.51 and state that they have no objection if 20% negligence of the deceased be considered, however, the Tribunal has decided sole negligence of the jeep driver,
which is perverse.

He has submitted that on one hand, the Tribunal has observed about Exh.51 purshis i.e. acceptance of negligence on the part of the deceased and on the other hand, the Tribunal has held jeep driver sole negligent.
He has submitted that the impugned judgment and award may be modified to that extent only and the amount may be refunded accordingly.

4. Per contra, Mr. S.R. Rathod and Mr.Hemal Shah, learned advocates for the contesting respondents - original claimants has submitted that the Tribunal has rightly observed about the negligence part and rightly considered the sole negligence of the jeep driver, as it was a head-on collision and jeep came in full speed as per the statement of Bhaveshbhai produced at Exh.37.
They have submitted that the impugned judgment and award is just and proper and no interference may be made.
They have submitted that this appeal may be dismissed.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4759/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined 5.
It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6.1 I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

From the record, it transpires that the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.15,43,600/- by considering the income, prospective income, deduction of personal expenses and multiplier as well as general and non-pecuniary damages as per the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court, which is just and proper and no interference is required.
However, here, the question is about negligence.

The contention of the learned advocate for the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4759/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined appellant - insurance company is that, as per the purshis given by the learned advocate for the claimants before the Tribunal at Exh.51 that they have no objection if negligence of the deceased be considered to the extent 20% qua the accident in question, even though the Tribunal has held sole negligence of the jeep driver.

Therefore, if we consider the negligence of the deceased to the extent 20% as per the purshis given by the learned advocate for the claimants before the Tribunal, under the circumstances, the total amount of compensation would be reduced to that extent only.

This Court has perused the impugned judgment The United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Jiviben Jayeshbhai Nandaniya on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51287009/
3 and award passed by the Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has considered the documents available on record.

This Court finds that once the claimants themselves have accepted negligence of the deceased to the extent 20% by way of a purshis produced on record at Exh.51 before the Tribunal, the Tribunal ought to have considered the said purshis while deciding negligence and awarding compensation.

Therefore, it should be considered and the negligence apportioned by the Tribunal is required to be modified to the extent that the jeep driver is held negligence to the extent 80% and the deceased is held negligence to the extent 20% qua the accident in question.

Since there is no dispute with regard to the income, loss of dependency and general and non-pecuniary damages decided and awarded by the Tribunal, this Court does not warrant NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4759/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined any interference qua it and the same remains unaltered.
6.2 Therefore, total compensation would be as under, which the claimant/s is/are entitled to get.
Particulars A  Total awarded amount   Less : 20% negligence of the deceased   Amount which is to be refunded  7.

Therefore, I hold that the claimant/s is/are entitled to get the total amount of compensation as mentioned hereinabove, which would meet the ends of justice.
8.
For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The appeal is partly allowed.

8.2 The Insurance Company is entitled to get refund of Rs.3,08,720/- with interest and cost, if any,
as decided by the Tribunal.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4759/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined 8.3

The Tribunal shall refund the amount of Rs.3,08,720/- with interest and cost, if any, to the appellant - insurance company, by account payee cheque / NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.

8.4 The Tribunal shall disburse rest of the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest and cost thereon, if any, to the claimants,
by account payee cheque / NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
8.5 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
8.6 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J) M.H. DAVE The United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Jiviben Jayeshbhai Nandaniya on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51287009/
